questions.stem: Which number is read as 'One Lakh' in the Indian place value system?
questions.solution: In the Indian place value system, 1,00,000 is read as 'One Lakh' because it represents one hundred thousand. The other options do not match this value: 1,000 is one thousand, 10,000 is ten thousand, and 1,000,000 is one million, which is much larger.

questions.stem: How many lakhs make a billion?
questions.solution: A billion is equal to 10,000 lakhs. The other options do not represent the correct conversion between lakhs and billions.

questions.stem: What is the number name of 9,87,65,01,234 in the Indian system?
choices: Nine arab eighty-seven crore sixty-five lakh one thousand two hundred thirty-four
Nine crore eighty-seven lakh sixty-five thousand one hundred twenty-three
Nine thousand eight hundred seventy-six crore fifty lakh one thousand two hundred thirty-four

questions.solution: The number 9,87,65,01,234 in the Indian system is read as 'Nine arab eighty-seven crore sixty-five lakh one thousand two hundred thirty-four'. questions.stem: If a single sheet of paper weighs 5 grams, how much would 1 lakh sheets of paper weigh?
questions.solution: 1 lakh sheets of paper would weigh 5,00,000 grams. Each sheet weighs 5 grams, so 1,00,000 × 5 = 5,00,000 grams. The other options are incorrect as they do not correctly compute the total weight.

questions.stem: How many times does the digit 7 occur in the number N = 6 + 66 + 666 + · · · + 666 · · · 66, where there are hundred 6’s in the last term?
questions.solution: The sum of the series can be calculated by recognizing a pattern in the digits. When the series is expanded and added, the digit 7 appears exactly 12 times due to the carry-over effects in each place value. The option 10 is incorrect because it misses some carry-overs, 11 is also incorrect for the same reason, and 13 is incorrect because it overestimates the number of 7s.

questions.stem: If a grey-headed albatross can travel 900–1000 km in a day, how many days would it take to complete a 12,000 km trip?
questions.solution: If the albatross travels 900 km per day, it would take approximately 13.3 days, and if it travels 1000 km per day, it would take 12 days. Thus, the trip would take approximately 12 to 14 days. The other options do not accurately represent the range of days based on the given speeds.
